title: The Uncharted Rivergate
premise: Marguerite Winterbourne has spent a decade avoiding her late father's unfinished obsession: the Rivergate, a drowned temple complex upriver in the monsoon country where he vanished. When his old rival, Edmund Voss, hires her crew with proof that the site will be dynamited for a dam within months, she takes the job to reach it first and burn whatever evidence could justify the excavation. But Voss's men follow them into the flood season, her leaking boat strands her with Callum Reyes—a cartographer with his own debt to Voss—and together they must survive the monsoon, outwit the hired guns, and decide whether her father's legacy is worth dying for. In the end, Marguerite floods the dig herself, sealing the Rivergate forever, and chooses Callum and a life above ground over the inheritance that nearly killed her.
about_author: Jonah Hartwell is a former river guide who spent six seasons running cargo through monsoon country before turning to fiction full-time. His novels are known for their brutal landscapes, morally tangled crews, and heroes who learn that survival is rarely free.

chapters.title: The Weight of Dry Ground
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She runs a small survey crew in the delta lowlands, keeping deliberately beneath the radar of academic circles. A letter arrives bearing her father's handwriting—posthumous, forwarded by Voss. The beat: unease; the past has found an address.

chapters.title: An Offer from the Other Side
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Voss visits her camp, offering triple pay to lead a salvage survey of the Rivergate before a government dam project floods the valley permanently. He shows her her father's final field notes. She refuses—and then reads the notes all night. Beat: temptation wrapped in grief.

chapters.title: Crew of Strays
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She assembles her team: gruff boatman Odile, young tech Sefu, and medic Priya, each carrying their own reasons to say yes to dangerous money. They sign on knowing the season is wrong. Beat: wary camaraderie forged over maps and bad coffee.

chapters.title: The Stranger at the Dock
chapters.summary: Callum's POV introduced. He appears claiming to be a hydrologist hired by Voss, but Marguerite catches him photographing her father's notes. She lets him aboard anyway, needing another pair of hands. Beat: mutual suspicion disguised as politeness.

chapters.title: Upriver
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The journey begins through narrowing gorges; Odile warns the monsoon is early this year. First signs they're followed: a second engine at night, never seen by daylight. Beat: dread accumulating like storm clouds.

chapters.title: What Her Father Left Behind
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. At an abandoned waystation she finds a cache her father hid decades ago—letters revealing he believed the Rivergate held records of a civilization that chose to drown itself rather than be conquered. Beat: awe curdling into understanding of his obsession.

chapters.title: Leak
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. The boat springs a serious leak in rapids; they beach it, losing two days of supplies. Callum admits fragments of his truth: he mapped the valley for Voss years ago and owes him a debt he can't name aloud. Beat: confession under pressure.

chapters.title: The First Marker
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. They find her father's last survey marker, fresh rope still tied to it—he was here alive after his official disappearance date. Someone else knows. That night the followers strike the camp, stealing the field notes. Beat: violation and fury.

chapters.title: Monsoon Makes Landfall
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV rotation. The rains arrive days early, stranding everyone. The stolen notes turn up torn along the riverbank—one of their own took them. Suspicion poisons the crew. Beat: trust fracturing as water rises.

chapters.title: The Drowned Stair
chapters.summary: Marguerite and Callum's shared POV chapters begin. Rising water reveals the top of a submerged stone stair—the true entrance her father sought. They descend briefly before flooding forces retreat. Beat: wonder and terror in equal measure.

chapters.title: Odile's Bargain
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Confronted, Odile confesses: Voss holds her brother's debts; she copied the notes but couldn't hand them over whole. Marguerite must decide between exile and forgiveness. Beat: the price of survival made personal.

chapters.title: Voss Arrives
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Voss's expedition boats appear, well-provisioned, armed, and led by a man who speaks of her father with genuine love and genuine ruthlessness. He offers partnership one last time. Beat: the enemy revealed as a mirror.

chapters.title: High Water
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. A flash flood sweeps the lower camp; Priya saves Sefu but the fuel stores are lost. Both expeditions are now trapped on the same ridge until waters drop. Uneasy coexistence. Beat: survival forcing enemies together.

chapters.title: Letters in the Flood
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Trapped in a cave shelter, she reads her father's letters aloud to the combined camps—including Voss. His final entry says the Rivergate should stay drowned, and asks whoever finds it to let it rest. Beat: grief transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Map Callum Hid
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. Marguerite discovers Callum's original survey—the precise map Voss needs to blast the temple safely. His debt: Voss holds evidence that would imprison Callum's sister. Betrayal cuts deeper because it was love-shaped. Beat: heartbreak at the worst hour.

chapters.title: Two Fires
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Voss's men move to secure the entrance before the peak flood; Marguerite's crew sabotages their explosives cache. A fire fight in the rain leaves Sefu wounded and one of Voss's men dead. Beat: no clean hands left.

chapters.title: The Descent
chapters.summary: Marguerite and Callum's POV. With hours before the valley floods completely, Marguerite descends alone to place charges of her own—to bury the site beyond recovery. Callum follows against her orders. Beat: duty and love pulling opposite directions.

chapters.title: Inside the Rivergate
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The flooded halls hold her father's final camp, his skeleton at a desk of clay tablets—the records of a people who chose the water over conquest. She understands him fully at last, and forgives him. Beat: catharsis in the dark.

chapters.title: Voss's Choice
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. He follows her down, gun drawn, but stands before the tablets and cannot give the order. The man who loved her father weeps in a drowning temple. He lets her set the charges. Beat: the antagonist's humanity breaking through.

chapters.title: Let It Rest
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The charges bring the ceiling down as the monsoon peak surges in; Callum drags her out as the Rivergate collapses into permanent oblivion. Voss's crew evacuates without him ordering pursuit. Beat: sacrifice completed, survival barely earned.

chapters.title: Afterwater
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. The survivors regroup downstream; Voss releases Callum's sister's file unprompted, saying some debts die with the men who hold them. Odile stays with Voss's crew as penance and peace. Beat: quiet accounting of what remains.

chapters.title: The Uncharted Rivergate
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, epilogue tone. Months later, the dam reservoir fills; maps mark nothing where the temple sleeps. Marguerite and Callum charter a small boat toward open coast—not running now, but choosing. Beat: love chosen freely over inheritance, and peace earned the hard way.
